title: Chapter 1: The Toolbox for a Data Scientist
text:
To be a data scientist, you don’t just need to know math; you need to know how to use the “tools of the trade.”






TipWhy this matters for MAT 186



According to our course outline (ECO), mastering GitHub is not just about storage—it is about Reproducibility, a core pillar of modern data science.




Before we install the software, let’s look at the path data takes from a raw file to a finished report.

title: MAT 186: Introduction to Data Science
text: Welcome to the official OER Lecture Notes for MAT 186. These materials are designed to provide a theoretical and practical foundation in Data Science using R and Quarto.

title: MAT 186: Introduction to Data Science
text:
Course Goals

Master the Data Science workflow (Import, Tidy, Transform, Visualize, Model, Communicate).
Build reproducible reports using Quarto and GitHub.
Apply statistical inference to real-world datasets.

title: Chapter 2: R Programming Foundations
text:
NoteLearning Objectives (ECO Alignment)



By the end of this chapter, you will be able to: 1. Identify and create different R object types (Vectors, Data Frames). 2. Use functions and arguments to manipulate data. 3. Install and load R packages via the Tidyverse.



Introduction to R
R is more than a calculator; it is an object-oriented language. In Data Science, we store our data in objects so we can transform and visualize them efficiently.

title: ECO Alignment & Learning Objectives
text:
Detailed Module Breakdown

Module 1: Foundational Tools
ECO Topic: Setup of data science environment and version control. Learning Objective: Students will demonstrate proficiency in using R, RStudio, and GitHub for reproducible research.

OER Implementation: Chapter 1: The Toolbox
Lab Integration: Directly supports Lab 1 by providing the theoretical “why” behind reproducibility and GitHub.
References: R for Data Science (2e), Chapter 1.



Module 2: R Programming
ECO Topic: Programming foundations, functions, and packages. Learning Objective: Students will write functions and utilize R packages to process data.

OER Implementation: Chapter 2: R Programming Foundations
Lab Integration: Provides the syntax foundations required for Lab 2 (objects, vectors, and library loading).
References: Hands-On Programming with R, Parts 1 & 2.
